semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {فُجِّرَتْ}: The majority read it in the passive with doubling. Mujāhid read it in the active without doubling, from al-fujūr (transgressing bounds), with regard to His saying {بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لاَّ يَبْغِيَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 20]: when the barrier is removed, they transgress. Mujāhid also, al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, al-Zaʿfarānī and al-Thawrī read it in the passive without doubling.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {بُعْثِرَتْ}: i.e. overturned. One says baʿtharahu and baḥtharahu, with ʿayn and with ḥāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They are compounded from al-baʿth (raising) and al-baḥth (searching), with a rāʾ joined to them." He means that they are among words whose meanings agree, because the rāʾ is added in them even though it is not one of the augment letters; this is like damith and dimathr, and sabiṭa and sibaṭr. «عَلِمَتْ» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا».

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {مَا غَرَّكَ}: The majority read «غَرَّك» as a triliteral, with «ما» interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read «ما أَغَرَّك»; it may then be interrogative or exclamatory. The meaning of agharrahu («أغرَّه») is: made him enter into heedlessness (al-ghirra), or made him heedless.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَكَ}: It admits following [the preceding noun] as a badal (substitute), as explication (bayān) or as a naʿt (adjective), and severance (qaṭʿ) to the nominative or the accusative.
His saying: {فَعَدَلَكَ}: The Kufans read «عَدَلَك» without doubling, and the rest / with doubling. The doubled form means: He made you proportionate in your limbs, so He did not make one of your hands or feet longer, nor one of your eyes wider; it is from al-taʿdīl (proportioning). The reading without doubling admits this, i.e. He balanced some of your limbs with others; and it may be from al-ʿudūl (turning), i.e. He turned you to whatever He willed of forms, shapes and likenesses.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {في أَىِّ صُورَةٍ}: Several views are possible concerning it. The first: that it is attached to «رَكَّبَكَ», «ما» being redundant (zāʾida) on this view, and «شاءَ» an adjective of «صورةٍ». He did not conjoin «رَكَّبَكَ» to what precedes it with the fāʾ, as He conjoined what precedes it with it, because it is an explication of His saying «فَعَدَلَكَ». The implied form is: He proportioned you: He assembled you in whatever form He willed of the wondrous, beautiful forms. The meaning is: He placed you in a form that His will required: of beauty and ugliness, tallness and shortness, maleness and femaleness. The second: that it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He assembled you, being in one of the forms. The third: that it is attached to «عَدَلَكَ»; the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted this from some interpreters and did not object to it. But it is open to objection, in that «أيّ» contains the meaning of interrogation and so has the head of the sentence; how then can what precedes it govern it?
It is as though al-Zamakhsharī sensed this, for he said: "«أيّ» has the meaning of wonder, i.e. He proportioned you in what a wondrous form!" This cannot well justify the governing word preceding the interrogative noun, even if the meaning of wonder has entered it. Do you not see that «كيف» and «أنَّى», even if the meaning of wonder enters them, do not have their governing word placed before them? The grammarians disagreed concerning the interrogative noun when confirmation (istithbāt) is intended by it: may its governing word precede it or not? The correct view is that it may not. Likewise, the governing word of declarative «كم» may not precede it, because of its resemblance in form to the interrogative; so this is all the more so. On its being attached to «عَدَلَكَ», «ما» is accusative by «شاء», i.e. He assembled you in whatever assembling He willed, i.e. a beautiful assembling; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Its apparent sense is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (absolute object).
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ما» may be redundant, or it may be conditional; on both, the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «صورة» and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. He assembled you upon it. And «في» is attached to «رَكَّبك». It was also said: the clause has no position, because «في» is attached to one of the two verbs and the whole is one utterance; the interrogative only precedes «ما» because that is its right." His saying "to one of the two verbs" means «شاءَ» and «رَكَّبك». So three aspects result for «ما»: redundancy; being conditional, in which case its apodosis is omitted; and being accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. standing in the place of a maṣdar.

semin-durr:9-9.t: The majority read «يُكَذِّبُون» as address «[Translator's note: so in the text; the address reading is «تُكَذِّبُون»]». Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with the yāʾ of the third person.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ}: The clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تُكَذِّبون», i.e. you deny while this is the situation; or it may be resumptive: He informed them of that so that they would desist.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {يَعْلَمُونَ}: It may be a naʿt (adjective), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «كاتبين», or a naʿt of «جحيم», or resumptive.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {يَصْلَوْنَهَا}: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase, since it serves as khabar (predicate); or it may be resumptive. The majority read «يَصْلَوْنَها» without doubling, in the active, and Ibn Miqsam with doubling, in the passive. Its like has preceded.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ لاَ تَمْلِكُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يوم» in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the day". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a badal (substitute) for what precedes it, meaning His saying «يومَ الدين». Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «يومٌ» nominative with tanwīn, cutting it off from the iḍāfa (genitive construct) and making the clause an adjective of it, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "on which [no soul] has power". The rest read «يومَ» with fatḥa. It was said: it is a fatḥa of iʿrāb, and it is accusative by an implied «أعني» or «يتجاوزون», or by an implied «اذكُرْ», so that it is a direct object. According to the view of the Kufans it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ and was only made indeclinable (mabnī) because of its iḍāfa to the verb, even though [the verb] is declinable, like His saying {هذا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ} [al-Māʾida: 119]; this has preceded.
